title: Immigrants in Finance: Evidence from Hedge Funds
authors: Jun Chen; Shenje Hshieh; Melvyn Teo; Feng Zhang
eligible_reason: No qualifying staggered binary design. (i) The H-1B lottery DiD (Table 5, Figure 2, Tables 9-10) is a stacked design: 09_create_dataset_fig02_tables05_09_10.R builds a stacked panel of +/-36 months around each January lottery year (shockdt), with fundXshock and shockXyrmo FE, propensity-score-matched controls and match1cnt analytic weights, plus time-varying controls logassetsL1 fundageL1 (stacked-only, matching weights: not eligible). (ii) Table 6 DiD (treatXpost) uses a single common date: 04_create_hedgefund_variables.do line 408 sets post = (yr >= 2004) for all funds (FY2004 H-1B cap cut), treated = fund ever used H-1B; one adoption cohort, plus time-varying controls. (iii) Tables 2, 3, 7, 8 regress returns on continuous or count H-1B measures (pct_demandmet, all_129_yrmo_rk) or interactions with them; Tables 11-12 are probit/OLS cross-sectional determinants. Shipped data are pseudo datasets (README), so the paper would be excluded on data grounds in any case.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe and R fixest. Table 5: reghdfe raw_ret/alpha24mo c.splitgrp##c.postlot logassetsL1 fundageL1 [aw=match1cnt], absorb(fundXshock shockXyrmo) cluster(firmXshock), stacked lottery cohorts with PS-matched controls. Table 6: reghdfe y treatXpost logassetsL1 fundageL1, absorb(fundgrp yrmo) cluster(firmgrp), SAMPLE_DID 2001-2006, post = yr>=2004. Figure 3 is a collapsed treated-vs-control residual plot around 2004m1.
main_or_robustness: main (lottery stacked DiD is the main identification)
data_files_note: README: 'we provide all intermediate pseudo datasets ... We also provide the pseudo datasets (in the data_output folder) from which the results in the paper are produced.' Original TASS/HFR/Morningstar and I-129 FOIA data are not shared; logs on original data shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Lottery DiD is stacked with PS-matched weights; the only unstacked DiD has a single post date (2004). Data are pseudo.
